I am 57 years old, I never went to school, cannot read. But I have farmed this land for 25 years, and my mother taught me before that. I have 9.8 mu, not big, not small. My son works in the factory in Handan, my daughter-in-law helps sometimes, but mostly it is me. I have a well, so I can irrigate when the water is low.

For my wheat, I do what I did last year. I buy the improved wheat seeds from the shop in town — 25 jin per mu, I think it is Jinmai or something, the white seeds. Before sowing in October, I hire the rotary machine to turn the soil. Then I put one big bag of compound fertilizer on each mu — that is 100 jin per mu. The bag says 18-18-18 or something, the shopkeeper picks it. That is my base fertilizer. Then in March, when the wheat is waking up, I spread another half bag of urea on each mu — about 50 jin per mu. If the weather looks dry, maybe a bit more. I know it costs money, but last year I put less and my wheat was thin. I cannot risk that. Better to waste a little fertilizer than cry at harvest.

I irrigate three times for wheat: once in winter so the wheat does not freeze dry, once in spring when it is growing fast, and once when the grain is filling. I spray four times — herbicide once before winter, insecticide twice in spring, and fungicide once when the heads come out. Everyone around here does about the same. I expect 1000 jin per mu, maybe 1100 if the rain is good. Last year I got about 1000 jin.

For maize, after I cut the wheat in June, I have no time to plough deep. I hire the no-till seeder to put the hybrid maize seeds straight into the wheat stubble. I buy new hybrid seeds every year — 3 jin per mu, the yellow kind. I put down 80 jin of compound fertilizer per mu as base, and then when the maize is knee-high, I topdress with 40 jin of urea per mu. I know some people put more, but maize is stronger than wheat. I irrigate twice — once if June is dry, and once when the tassels come out. I spray three times: herbicide once when the maize is small, insecticide twice because the worms come every year. I expect around 1100 to 1200 jin per mu for maize.

Everything costs money. The compound fertilizer is expensive now, over 150 yuan per bag. Urea is also up. But if I cut back and the yield drops, I lose more than I save. I watch what my neighbors do. If Lao Wang puts one bag per mu, I put one bag per mu. We all talk in the field. That is how I know what to do.
